turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - nlo_dn_train.csv: 200 crystalline materials, columns `formula`, `poscar`
    (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format) and `dn` (the birefringence at
    1064 nm, dimensionless).
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

Using the training data, predict each candidate's birefringence at 1064 nm,
then select the 5 candidates whose birefringence is CLOSEST to 0.1.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, closest first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
I used structure-sensitive analog matching, emphasizing composition, cation ordering, lattice symmetry, and anisotropy. Cubic candidates were assigned near-zero birefringence, consistent with the training data. The closest predictions to 0.1 are:

| Rank | candidate_id | Predicted \(dn\) | \(|dn-0.1|\) | Main structural analogs |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | c071 | 0.1015 | 0.0015 | Ga–Cu–Ge–Se and In–Cu–Ge–Se chalcopyrite-like structures |
| 2 | c056 | 0.0974 | 0.0026 | In–Cu–Ge–Se and In–Ag–Sn–Se compounds |
| 3 | c098 | 0.1041 | 0.0041 | Low-symmetry Li–Mg–Ga–Se structures clustered around 0.09–0.12 |
| 4 | c066 | 0.0948 | 0.0052 | Hexagonal Y–Ag–Te structures, adjusted for Ag→Cu |
| 5 | c082 | 0.1082 | 0.0082 | Ga–Hg–Se and Al–Hg–S chalcopyrite-like analogs |

These estimates have appreciable uncertainty—roughly \(0.01\)–\(0.03\)—but the selected structures have the strongest local correspondence to training materials near the target.

Final: c071, c056, c098, c066, c082
